clue.text: No good making a mess of sweet food

indicators.note: 'No good' tells us to drop the abbreviation for good from the word before it

parts.note: muffing is botching or making a mess of something

explanation.surface: A cook bungles a dessert, producing something no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' signals removal: MUFFING without its G.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffin is a small baked cake, often sweet, eaten as a treat.

clue.text: See 2
Legal exemption from fee juror came to settle

indicators.note: to settle suggests the letters are arranged into a new resolved order

explanation.surface: A juror who has arrived is released from paying a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Force majeure is a contract clause freeing a party from liability when an unforeseeable event intervenes.

clue.text: Trendy pop for European royalty

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
Fanta is a brand of fizzy soft drink, or pop

explanation.surface: A fashionable fizzy drink suitable for a royal.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese king.

clue.text: Old Testament sermoniser who's with his God?

definitions.text: Old Testament sermoniser who's with his God?

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest at Shiloh who taught the young Samuel
Jah is a short form of Jehovah, the Hebrew name of God

explanation.surface: A question about a biblical preacher keeping company with the deity.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI with JAH; the whole clue also describes the prophet, who was carried up to heaven in a whirlwind and so is with his God.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is a prophet of the Old Testament books of Kings who preached against Baal worship.

clue.text: What could bore reading Twitter!

parts.note: a lathe is a machine tool that can bore holes
reading is one of the three Rs, so it gives R

explanation.surface: Reading social media posts can be very tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' and 'Twitter' suggest dull social media; a twitter is also a nervous fluster.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a lather or a twitter both mean being in a state of agitation.

clue.text: Athlete's bits held up by this?

definitions.text: Athlete's bits held up by this?

parts.note: a jock is slang for a sporty athlete

indicators.note: held up in a down entry means the word for bits reads from bottom to top

parts.note: parts are bits or pieces

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about what supports a sportsman's private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTS turned upwards gives STRAP; the whole clue also describes the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockstrap is a supporter worn by male athletes to hold the genitals.

clue.text: Having pawned donkey, get cushion?

indicators.note: having means holding, so one word contains the other

parts.note: in hock means pawned
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: After pawning a donkey, someone buys a cushion.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassock is a firm cushion for kneeling on in church.

clue.text: In central London, stop men going on the game

indicators.note: going on means the game is placed after the men

parts.note: knights are chess men
bridge is the card game

explanation.surface: A call in central London for men to stop working as prostitutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the game' suggests prostitution; Knightsbridge is a district and Underground stop in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Knightsbridge is an Underground station, a stop on the Piccadilly line in London.

clue.text: Open government Australia's brought back

indicators.note: brought back says these pieces are written from right to left

parts.note: the Raj was British rule in India, so raj can mean government
A is the abbreviation for Australia, as on international vehicle plates

explanation.surface: Open government returning to Australia, as a political news item.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is said to be standing ajar.

clue.text: Initiator of frenzy — maniac's maddened with it

definitions.text: Initiator of frenzy — maniac's maddened with it

indicators.note: the initiator of a word is the letter that starts it
maddened says the letters of the following words are driven into a crazy new order

explanation.surface: A maniac whipped up into a frenzy describes extreme zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: F, then MANIACSIT rearranged by 'maddened' to give ANATICISM; the whole clue is also a picture of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanaticism is excessive, frenzied zeal, the state of a maniac carried away by a cause.

clue.text: Go without drug twice! Is it pot?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the first word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in taking turns at a game

indicators.note: twice says the drug's letter is used two times

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone abstaining from drugs asks whether cannabis counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go without drug' reads as abstinence, but 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'pot' is a cooking vessel, not cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: A tureen is a deep lidded serving dish, a kind of pot for soup.

clue.text: Steady with the yoga — one's in a funny position

indicators.note: letters put in a funny position are rearranged, as a yoga pose twists the body

explanation.surface: A yoga teacher urges caution to a pupil contorted into an odd pose.
explanation.definitionFit: To go easy on something is to use it sparingly, holding steady with it rather than overdoing it.

clue.text: 10, say, has fresh air

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters are made new by being rearranged

parts.note: the number 10 written as a word is ten

explanation.surface: A reference to another clue, a number with some fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across, but it just means TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, and a sea shanty is a traditional sailors' work song.

clue.text: Bit of cash gambler finally raised for flirty girl

parts.note: a sou was a French coin of small value

indicators.note: the final letter of the gambler word is lifted higher up in this down entry

parts.note: a better is one who bets

explanation.surface: A gambler who finally put up a bit of money for a flirtatious girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally raised' lifts the last letter R of BETTER to become BRETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A soubrette is a pert, coquettish maid role in comedy or opera.

clue.text: Tramp — one missing current English king

indicators.note: missing says the current's word is taken away from the word before

parts.note: one points back to the word just given, so it stands for tramp itself
an amp is a unit of electric current, here written as the word amp
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A vagrant who lacks money, plus some talk of an English monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'Tramp': lose AMP from TRAMP to leave TR, then add E and K.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk a long way with heavy steps, which is what a trek involves.

clue.text: Minnow from Conservative HQ

parts.note: a hub is a central headquarters

explanation.surface: A minor figure emerging from the Conservative party's headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minnow' suggests a political nobody, but here it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family, to which minnows belong.

clue.text: Least macho punters here on trial

indicators.note: on means one piece follows the other in this down entry

parts.note: punters push punts on the River Cam in Cambridge
a trial is a troublesome person, a pest

explanation.surface: Gamblers here are on trial, with no machismo about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punters' suggests gamblers; here they are people punting boats on the Cam, Cambridge's river.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp means effeminate or theatrical, so the most camp is the least macho.

clue.text: I steer powerboat around Britain's old Scottish ground

indicators.note: around tells us the first pieces are placed on either side of Britain's letters

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated bull, so an ox
Br is an old abbreviation for British
split as power and boat: P is the physics symbol for power, and Noah's ark was a boat

explanation.surface: Someone piloting a fast boat round Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerboat' splits into P and ARK. IBROX PARK is the home ground of Rangers football club in Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibrox Park is a football stadium in Glasgow, a ground in the sporting sense.

clue.text: Unacceptable prune's hard, protruding part

parts.note: out can mean not acceptable or out of the question
to crop is to trim or prune

explanation.surface: A dried plum's tough stalk is not to be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is rock that sticks out from the ground, hard and protruding.

clue.text: Soldiers question the protection they have

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to question something is to doubt it

explanation.surface: Troops query whether their defences are adequate.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small fort, defensive shelter available to soldiers.

clue.text: America, burning, cheers up invader

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: lit means alight or burning
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A fiery America toasts an invading force.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila was the fifth-century leader of the Huns who invaded the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Romantic figures given increasingly sober, splendid clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, meaning one piece dresses around the other

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or splendid, written with the letter I for the figure one
more TT, where TT means teetotal

explanation.surface: Romantic people dressing in fine clothes as they drink less.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoretti are little cupids, figures of love in art.

clue.text: Like the rural upper classes getting back in hunt — pathetic!

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: weedy means feeble or pathetic

explanation.surface: Posh country folk returning to hunting, dismissed as pathetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweedy describes the country gentry, who traditionally wear tweed suits.

clue.text: Two characters, both Poles, in European city

parts.note: the two letters S and N, abbreviations for the south and north poles, spelt out as words
the two letters S and N, abbreviations for the south and north poles, spelt out as words

explanation.surface: A pair of Polish people living in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland; they are the magnetic poles south and north, whose letters are spelt ess and en.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of Germany.

clue.text: Footballer in red

definitions.meaning: a forward who plays on the left wing of the pitch
a red is a socialist or communist, someone of the political left

explanation.surface: A soccer player wearing a red kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers both a wide forward on the left and a person of leftist politics.

clue.text: Clap, maybe, when welcoming university's boss

indicators.note: welcoming means taking another piece inside

parts.note: the clap is slang for gonorrhoea, an example of an STD
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Applause greeting the head of a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clap' looks like applause, but it is a slang name for a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a knob or raised ornament, and a stud is a similar decorative fastening.

clue.text: Queen single's piercing beat is something that really gets into your head!

definitions.text: something that really gets into your head

indicators.note: piercing means these pieces go inside the beat word

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen
an EP is an extended-play record, a kind of single

explanation.surface: A queen's hit record has a beat that sticks in your head.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an earworm; the definition is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trepan is a surgical instrument for boring holes in the skull, so it truly gets into your head.

clue.text: One's played head of police in crime film

indicators.note: in places the police letter inside the crime word

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing or crime

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A police chief is portrayed by an actor in a crime movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's played' looks like an actor's role, but it is an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, an instrument that someone plays.
